subject: chemistry
title: Metals vs Non-metals
welcome_lead: Shiny, bendy, buzzing with current: meet the metallic family.
meta_desc: Compare metals and non-metals in this KS3 chemistry adventure on physical properties.
final_note: You can now classify any element as a metal or non-metal by its properties.

concepts.def: Shiny, conducts heat and electricity, malleable.
Dull, poor conductor, often brittle if solid.
Can be hammered into shape without breaking.
Allows heat or electricity to flow through it.
Does not let heat or electricity flow easily.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Most metals are shiny, good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable (bendable) and ductile (can be drawn into wires).

Most are solid at room temperature, with high melting points. Mercury is the exception — it is a liquid metal!

Non-metals are usually dull, poor conductors (insulators), and often brittle if solid. Many are gases at room temperature.

Examples: oxygen, sulfur, carbon, chlorine.

Copper wires carry electricity — they are a great conductor. Plastic around the wire is a great insulator and keeps you safe.

Match the property to the job.
